label: first copy steps of very short sequences (L=3, or L=4 first copy step)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase of short sequences. The strongest activations come from L=3 at the step just after <DEL> (input = orig 0, recall_idx 1). There it fires almost always (precision 0.97 for L=3 copy steps) and is largest, with weaker firing at recall_idx 2. For L=4 it fires weakly (low-quartile magnitudes) on about half of the recall_idx-1 steps (input orig 0 right after <DEL>), and rarely at recall_idx 2. Which L=4 sequences fire is token-dependent and not cleanly captured: it is more likely with no repeated or digit tokens and when the last original token is j/k/u/p/a, and top L=3 examples also often end in j/k. It never fires in the original phase, on the <DEL> step, at recall_idx 0, or for L>=5. Magnitude is mainly set by L (L=3 >> L=4) and then by recall_idx (1 > 2). The predicate covers 99% of activation mass, but precision (~0.64) is limited by the L=4 steps that do not fire.
